doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Tempo of rags and dance music, Joe Verges and Don't Leave Me Daddy
summary: Old dance tempos were slower; the talk moves to businessman's tempo and the writer of Don't Leave Me Daddy.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: What about tempo at that time? How fast would you play a rags? Not like they're playing today.
Oh, slow stuff. Mostly slow stuff. I mean, nothing. Medium fox tracks. Did you play frog legs? Just medium fox tracks. You ever play frog legs? Blues and stuff like that. That's what they played.
Sure, we played many. We played, though. We were the only bands playing all of the rags. The only.
You know? Now, could you beat off the time? I say, would you remember about the tempo you'd play maple leaf rags?
That was fast. That was fast.

Not like today. Like a two-step or one-step, you see? They were playing almost half as fast as what they're playing now. And then they'd play the blues and then the medium tempos in between because people used to dance then. Dance. Not what they do now.

That ain't dancing. Well, even in spots today in New York and a lot of cities, they get a certain tempo, what they call a businessman's tempo, and they never change it. They just keep that same tempo for the people on the floor. Oh, I wanted to tell you, Joe Virgis works across the street.
Remember the guy who wrote Don't Leave Me, Daddy? Jesus. He works across the street at night. He might be there at night. Invictus.

I saw him last in New York so many years ago, whether he'll remember, I don't know. Oh, yeah. His song is in the same house where I song, so. Oh, yeah. And I saw him up there and I said, alas, I didn't know he was still around.
Yeah, well, if you check in tonight, if you're in the neighborhood, go across the street and ask for Joe.
He's an old man, too. Oh, yeah, Joe.
But he talks about you, you know, and the different guys and all that.
Because we used to feature those songs, Don't Leave Me, Daddy.
